title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards by outlining its commitments to improve AI governance. It plans to develop new standards, regulations, and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and fair for the public.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The EU Regulation 2024/1689 establishes consistent rules for artificial intelligence across all member states, aiming to make AI safer, more transparent, and accountable. It also updates several existing regulations and directives, such as those on data protection, cybersecurity, and digital markets, to fit the new AI framework.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair, secure, and reliable. The policy offers guidance for exam boards and teachers to use AI responsibly while safeguarding the quality and trust of qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted material and evaluates the legal, economic, and societal impacts of that use. It offers guidance and recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection in the development of AI technologies.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” recognising the urgent need to tackle AI’s risks and harness its benefits. It outlines a commitment to strengthen regulation, boost investment in research, and promote responsible AI development to protect public trust and maintain national competitiveness.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will review how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, and it includes FAQs to clarify common questions about the process. It sets clear terms of reference that guide the committee’s evaluation of AI policies, ensuring they meet public expectations and recommending actions for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines the organization’s perspective on AI regulation, best practices, and policy recommendations.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping rules for medical products, focusing on ensuring safety, effectiveness, and ethical use. It outlines practical steps for regulators and manufacturers to adopt the AI White Paper principles in product development and oversight.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This policy outlines the Defence sector's plan to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI organization for its size. It focuses on building advanced AI capabilities that support defence objectives and maintain global leadership.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This policy outlines how the Department for Transport plans to collaborate with the transport industry to harness AI's benefits while addressing potential risks. It details strategies for partnership, governance, and safeguards to ensure safe and effective AI adoption in transport.
